# Data dictionary

Source: **Flickr tour datasets, Lim et al. (CIKM'16)**, <https://github.com/computationalmedia/tour-cikm16>
(`data/poi-Edin.csv`, `data/traj-Edin.csv`; Edinburgh). Built from geotagged Flickr photos.
The repository has **no licence file** (checked); it is used here for coursework only. Raw files are
copied to `data/raw/` and their SHA-256 sums are in `data/raw/CHECKSUMS.json`. Sizes: places 28 rows
(1 KB), trajectories 7 853 rows (~400 KB).

Legend: **R** = real (from the dataset), **D** = derived deterministically from real columns,
**G** = generated by us (assumption, not observed).

## Raw files (all R)

`poi-Edin.csv`

| column | meaning |
|---|---|
| poiID | place id (R) |
| poiCat | category: Cultural, Entertainment, Historical, Museum, Park, Structure (R) |
| poiLon, poiLat | coordinates (R) |

`traj-Edin.csv` (one row = one visit by one user)

| column | meaning |
|---|---|
| userID | Flickr user (R) — used to split train/val/test **by user** |
| trajID | trajectory id (R); ids are unique across users (checked) |
| poiID | place visited (R) |
| startTime, endTime | first / last photo timestamp at the place, Unix seconds (R) |
| #photo | photos taken there (R) |
| trajLen | number of places in the trajectory (R; matches the row count for 99.9 % of trajectories after the place filter) |
| poiDuration | endTime − startTime in seconds (R). **Noisy**: 68 % of visits are < 5 min because they have a single photo |

## Processed files (`python make_data.py`, seed 0)

`data/processed/Edin_places.csv`

| column | meaning | type |
|---|---|---|
| poi_idx | 0..24 index used by all models | D |
| poi_id, category, lon, lat | as raw | R |
| cat_idx | index of the category | D |
| n_visits | visits in the raw data | D |

Filter: keep places with **≥ 20 visits** (at most 60). Edinburgh: 28 → 25 places (ids 5, 6, 25 dropped).
Categories left: Structure 10, Historical 4, Park 4, Cultural 3, Museum 3, Entertainment 1.

`data/processed/Edin_visits.csv`

| column | meaning | type |
|---|---|---|
| user, traj, poi_idx | as raw (poi mapped to index) | R/D |
| pos_in_traj, traj_len | position and length **after** filtering | D |
| start_ts, end_ts, n_photo, duration_s | as raw | R |
| dur_clip_s | `clip(duration_s, 300, 14400)` — durations below 5 min raised to 5 min, above 4 h cut | **G** (rule) |
| hour_start, hour_end | clock hour of arrival / leaving = `(ts mod 86400)/3600 + 11` mod 24 | **G** (offset) |

*Why +11 h:* the stored timestamps are not local time. In all five cities photo activity peaks at the same
stored hour (03–04 h) and is lowest at 16–19 h; adding 11 h puts the trough at about 05 h and the peak at
about 15 h, which is plausible for sightseeing. This is an assumption, not a documented fact.

Other processing: visits sorted by (trajectory, start time); immediate repeats of the same place inside one
trajectory removed (none occurred); trajectories shortened by the place filter keep their remaining visits.
Result: 7 828 visits, 1 448 users, 5 009 trajectories, 2 819 consecutive-place transitions.

`data/processed/Edin_travel_min.npy` (25 × 25, **G**): walking minutes between places =
haversine distance × 1.3 (street detour factor) ÷ 4.5 km/h × 60. In the planner these are rounded to whole minutes.

`data/processed/Edin_meta.json`: all constants above.
`data/processed/Edin_splits_seed0.json`: users in train / val / test (70 / 15 / 15 %, seeded shuffle).

For goal-aware training examples (generated in memory by `goal_transitions`; not added to the CSV),
`goal_end` is the last POI in that filtered trajectory (derived from `poi_idx`), `stops_remaining`
is `traj_len - pos_in_traj - 1`, and `trajectory_position` is `pos_in_traj / max(traj_len - 1, 1)`.
These fields are derived from each real trajectory; they are not synthetic labels. Examples retain the
current place, hour, and next place from the real transition.

## Generated inputs of the experiments (all **G**)

| item | how it is generated |
|---|---|
| walking speed, detour | 4.5 km/h, ×1.3 (above) |
| number of stops | 4–8 in experiment 1, 4–10 in experiment 2, = real length (3–8) in experiment 3 |
| start / end place, must-see category, start hour | uniformly random with a fixed seed (experiments 1, 2: hour U(8,14), budget U(120,480) / U(60,400) min) |
| budget in experiment 3 | `max(real trajectory span, 30 min × stops)` where span = last end time − first start time |
| must-see in experiment 3 | category of a random intermediate stop of the real trajectory |
| stay time of a visit in the planner | `max(5, round(exp(predicted log duration)/60))` min; predicted by the duration NN |
